source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Public 2 Samuel 18:33 binds Hebrew 19:1; public 19:1–43 binds Hebrew 19:2–44. All other selected verses bind one-to-one to matching labels.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains renewed gathering and the full troop count.
verses.before: David again gathered all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.
verses.after: David again gathered Israel’s chosen men, thirty thousand of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: David again gathered all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.

verses.rationale: Preserves the doubled Name and difficult place expression.
verses.before: David arose and went with all the people who were with him from Baale-Judah to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the Name, the name of the LORD of Hosts who sits above the cherubim.
verses.after: He and everyone with him set out from Baale-judah to bring up the ark of God, which bears the Name—the name of the LORD of Armies, enthroned above the cherubim.
verses.tsw_comparator: David arose and went with all the people who were with him from Baale-Judah to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the Name, the name of the LORD of Hosts who sits above the cherubim.

verses.rationale: Keeps both sons, hill, and repeated new cart.
verses.before: They set the ark of God on a new cart and brought it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, sons of Abinadab, were driving the new cart.
verses.after: They put the ark of God on a new cart and brought it from Abinadab’s house on the hill. His sons Uzzah and Ahio drove the new cart.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set the ark of God on a new cart and brought it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, sons of Abinadab, were driving the new cart.

verses.rationale: Retains the compressed repetition without reconstructing a missing clause.
verses.before: They brought it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill, with the ark of God, and Ahio walked before the ark.
verses.after: They brought it from Abinadab’s house on the hill with the ark of God, and Ahio walked ahead of the ark.
verses.tsw_comparator: They brought it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill, with the ark of God, and Ahio walked before the ark.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned wood reference instead of importing with all their might.
verses.before: David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all kinds of instruments of cypress wood, with lyres, harps, tambourines, rattles, and cymbals.
verses.after: David and the whole house of Israel celebrated before the LORD with all kinds of cypress-wood instruments, with lyres, harps, tambourines, rattles, and cymbals.
verses.tsw_comparator: David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all kinds of instruments of cypress wood, with lyres, harps, tambourines, rattles, and cymbals.

verses.rationale: Makes the immediate cause clear; stumbling remains a qualified lexical choice.
verses.before: When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out toward the ark of God and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled.
verses.after: When they reached Nacon’s threshing floor, Uzzah reached toward the ark of God and took hold of it, because the oxen stumbled.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out toward the ark of God and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine agency; the rare offense term needs a note.
verses.before: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and God struck him there because of the irreverence, and he died there beside the ark of God.
verses.after: The LORD’s anger burned against Uzzah, and God struck him there for his irreverent act. He died there beside the ark of God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and God struck him there because of the irreverence, and he died there beside the ark of God.

verses.rationale: Connects the outbreak with its place-name and David’s anger.
verses.before: David was angry because the LORD had broken out against Uzzah, and that place has been called Perez-Uzzah to this day.
verses.after: David was angry because the LORD had broken out against Uzzah. He named that place Perez-uzzah, and it has that name to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: David was angry because the LORD had broken out against Uzzah, and that place has been called Perez-Uzzah to this day.

verses.rationale: Keeps fear distinct from the preceding anger.
verses.before: David was afraid of the LORD that day and said, “How can the ark of the LORD come to me?”
verses.after: That day David was afraid of the LORD. “How can the LORD’s ark come to me?” he asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: David was afraid of the LORD that day and said, “How can the ark of the LORD come to me?”

verses.rationale: Clarifies the change of destination and retains Gittite identity.
verses.before: So David was not willing to turn the ark of the LORD aside to himself into the city of David. Instead David turned it aside to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.
verses.after: David would not bring the LORD’s ark into the City of David. Instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
verses.tsw_comparator: So David was not willing to turn the ark of the LORD aside to himself into the city of David. Instead David turned it aside to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.

verses.rationale: Retains the duration and household-wide blessing.
verses.before: The ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-Edom and all his household.
verses.after: The LORD’s ark stayed in Obed-edom the Gittite’s house for three months, and the LORD blessed him and his whole household.
verses.tsw_comparator: The ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-Edom and all his household.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes reported blessing from David’s resulting action.
verses.before: It was told to King David, saying, “The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-Edom and all that belongs to him because of the ark of God.” So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-Edom into the city of David with rejoicing.
verses.after: King David was told, “The LORD has blessed Obed-edom’s household and everything he has because of the ark of God.” So David went and brought the ark up from Obed-edom’s house to the City of David with joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: It was told to King David, saying, “The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-Edom and all that belongs to him because of the ark of God.” So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-Edom into the city of David with rejoicing.

verses.rationale: Does not turn the six steps into a repeated interval.
verses.before: And it happened that when those carrying the ark of the LORD had gone six steps, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened animal.
verses.after: When those carrying the LORD’s ark had taken six steps, David sacrificed an ox and a fattened animal.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened that when those carrying the ark of the LORD had gone six steps, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened animal.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily movement, strength, and named garment.
verses.before: David was dancing with all his strength before the LORD, and David was girded with a linen ephod.
verses.after: David danced with all his strength before the LORD, wearing a linen ephod.
verses.tsw_comparator: David was dancing with all his strength before the LORD, and David was girded with a linen ephod.

verses.rationale: Preserves communal participation and distinct sound sources.
verses.before: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and with the sound of a ram’s horn.
verses.after: David and the whole house of Israel brought up the LORD’s ark with shouting and the sound of the ram’s horn.
verses.tsw_comparator: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and with the sound of a ram’s horn.

verses.rationale: Retains Michal’s relationship to Saul and her interior response.
verses.before: As the ark of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal daughter of Saul looked through the window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, and she despised him in her heart.
verses.after: As the LORD’s ark entered the City of David, Saul’s daughter Michal looked down through the window. She saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD and despised him in her heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: As the ark of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal daughter of Saul looked through the window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, and she despised him in her heart.

verses.rationale: Keeps tent placement and the two offering categories.
verses.before: They brought in the ark of the LORD and set it in its place among the tent that David had pitched for it. Then David offered burnt offerings and offerings of well-being before the LORD.
verses.after: They brought the LORD’s ark into the tent David had pitched for it and set it in its place. David offered burnt offerings and well-being offerings before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: They brought in the ark of the LORD and set it in its place in the midst of the tent that David had pitched for it. Then David offered burnt offerings and offerings of well-being before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the full divine title and sequence.
verses.before: When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the offerings of well-being, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: After finishing the burnt offerings and well-being offerings, David blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the offerings of well-being, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Retains both sexes and three gifts; date cake is uncertain.
verses.before: He distributed to all the people, to all the multitude of Israel, both man and woman, to each a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a raisin cake. Then all the people went, each to his house.
verses.after: He gave everyone in the entire crowd of Israel, men and women alike, a loaf of bread, a date cake, and a raisin cake. Then everyone went home.
verses.tsw_comparator: He distributed to all the people, to all the multitude of Israel, both man and woman, to each a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a raisin cake. Then all the people went, each to his house.

verses.rationale: Keeps sarcastic honor, exposure, and the women’s subordinate status.
verses.before: David returned to bless his household. Michal daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, “How honored the king of Israel made himself today, exposing himself today in the eyes of his servants’ slave women, as one of the empty men shamelessly exposes himself!”
verses.after: David returned to bless his household. Saul’s daughter Michal came out to meet him and said, “How Israel’s king has honored himself today! Exposing himself to his servants’ slave women as any shameless man might!”
verses.tsw_comparator: David returned to bless his household. Michal daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, “How honored the king of Israel made himself today, exposing himself today in the eyes of his servants’ slave women, as one of the empty men shamelessly exposes himself!”

verses.rationale: Retains the sharp comparison with Saul and repeated divine audience.
verses.before: David said to Michal, “It was before the LORD, who chose me over your father and over all his house to appoint me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel. Therefore I will celebrate before the LORD.
verses.after: David answered Michal, “It was before the LORD, who chose me over your father and his whole house and appointed me ruler of the LORD’s people Israel. I will celebrate before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to Michal, “It was before the LORD, who chose me over your father and over all his house to appoint me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel. Therefore I will celebrate before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves my own eyes and the contrast of contempt with honor.
verses.before: I will make myself even more lightly esteemed than this, and I will be low in my own eyes. But with the slave women of whom you spoke, with them I will be honored.”
verses.after: I will make myself still more contemptible than this, and lowly in my own eyes. But among the slave women you mentioned, I will be honored.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make myself even more lightly esteemed than this, and I will be low in my own eyes. But with the slave women of whom you spoke, with them I will be honored.”

verses.rationale: Does not add infertility, estrangement, or divine punishment as its cause.
verses.before: Michal daughter of Saul had no child until the day of her death.
verses.after: Saul’s daughter Michal had no child until the day she died.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Michal daughter of Saul had no child until the day of her death.

verses.rationale: Keeps the setting and rest motif across the verse boundary.
verses.before: When the king lived in his house and the LORD had given him rest from all his enemies around him,
verses.after: When the king was settled in his house and the LORD had given him rest from all his enemies around him,
verses.tsw_comparator: When the king lived in his house and the LORD had given him rest from all his enemies around him,

verses.rationale: Retains the contrast between royal house and movable curtains.
verses.before: the king said to Nathan the prophet, “See now, I live in a house of cedar, but the ark of God lives within tent curtains.”
verses.after: he said to the prophet Nathan, “Look, I live in a cedar house, but the ark of God stays inside tent curtains.”
verses.tsw_comparator: the king said to Nathan the prophet, “See now, I live in a house of cedar, but the ark of God lives within tent curtains.”

verses.rationale: Leaves this initial advice with Nathan, before the divine response.
verses.before: Nathan said to the king, “Go, do all that is in your heart, for the LORD is with you.”
verses.after: Nathan told the king, “Go ahead and do what is in your heart, for the LORD is with you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Nathan said to the king, “Go, do all that is in your heart, for the LORD is with you.”

verses.rationale: Makes the turn from advice to revelation audible.
verses.before: But that night the word of the LORD came to Nathan, saying,
verses.after: But that night the word of the LORD came to Nathan:
verses.tsw_comparator: But that night the word of the LORD came to Nathan, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves the rhetorical question and servant designation.
verses.before: “Go and say to my servant David: Thus says the LORD: Are you the one who will build me a house for my dwelling?
verses.after: “Go and tell my servant David, ‘This is what the LORD says: Are you the one to build a house for me to live in?
verses.tsw_comparator: “Go and say to my servant David: Thus says the LORD: Are you the one who will build me a house for my dwelling?

verses.rationale: Keeps both movable dwelling terms without implying two buildings.
verses.before: For I have not lived in a house from the day I brought up the children of Israel from Egypt until this day, but I have been moving about in a tent and dwelling.
verses.after: I have not lived in a house from the day I brought Israel out of Egypt until now. I have moved about in a tent, in a dwelling-place.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I have not lived in a house from the day I brought up the children of Israel from Egypt until this day, but I have been moving about in a tent and dwelling.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned tribes rather than substituting judges.
verses.before: In all the places where I moved about among all the children of Israel, did I speak a word with one of the tribes of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, saying, ‘Why have you not built me a house of cedar?’
verses.after: Wherever I moved among all Israel, did I ever ask any of Israel’s tribes, whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, “Why have you not built me a cedar house?”’
verses.tsw_comparator: In all the places where I moved about among all the children of Israel, did I speak a word with one of the tribes of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, saying, ‘Why have you not built me a house of cedar?’

verses.rationale: Preserves the movement from shepherding to ruling.
verses.before: “And now, thus you will say to my servant David: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler over my people, over Israel.
verses.after: “Now tell my servant David, ‘This is what the LORD of Armies says: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler over my people Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And now, thus you shall say to my servant David: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler over my people, over Israel.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes recalled protection from the promised great name.
verses.before: I have been with you wherever you went and have cut off all your enemies from before you. I will make for you a great name, like the name of the great ones who are on the earth.
verses.after: I have been with you wherever you went and have cut off all your enemies before you. I will make your name great, like the names of the great ones of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have been with you wherever you went and have cut off all your enemies from before you. I will make for you a great name, like the name of the great ones who are on the earth.

verses.rationale: Retains planting, settled place, and actual oppression.
verses.before: I will appoint a place for my people Israel and plant them, so that they may dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more. Violent people will no longer afflict them as formerly,
verses.after: I will provide a place for my people Israel and plant them there. They will live in their own place, disturbed no more. Violent people will no longer oppress them as they did before,
verses.tsw_comparator: I will appoint a place for my people Israel and plant them, so that they may dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more. Violent people shall no longer afflict them as formerly,

verses.rationale: Keeps the reversal from David building to receiving a house.
verses.before: from the day I appointed judges over my people Israel. I will give you rest from all your enemies. And the LORD declares to you that the LORD will make a house for you.
verses.after: ever since I appointed judges over my people Israel. I will give you rest from all your enemies. And the LORD declares to you that the LORD will make a house for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: from the day I appointed judges over my people Israel. I will give you rest from all your enemies. And the LORD declares to you that the LORD will make a house for you.

verses.rationale: Preserves death image, bodily descent, and singular successor.
verses.before: “When your days are fulfilled and you lie down with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring after you, who will come from your body, and I will establish his kingdom.
verses.after: When your days are complete and you lie down with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring after you, one born from your own body, and establish his kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: “When your days are fulfilled and you lie down with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring after you, who will come from your body, and I will establish his kingdom.

verses.rationale: Keeps house, name, throne, and perpetual promise distinct.
verses.before: He will build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
verses.after: He will build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.

verses.rationale: Retains familial relation and bodily discipline without spiritualizing blows.
verses.before: I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me. When he commits wrong, I will discipline him with a rod of men and with blows of the children of humanity.
verses.after: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I will correct him with a human rod and with blows from human hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will be a father to him, and he shall be a son to me. When he commits wrong, I will discipline him with a rod of men and with blows of the children of humanity.

verses.rationale: Preserves the contrast with Saul rather than an unconditional moral approval.
verses.before: But my steadfast love will not depart from him as I removed it from Saul, whom I removed from before you.
verses.after: But my steadfast love will not leave him as I took it away from Saul, whom I removed from before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But my steadfast love shall not depart from him as I removed it from Saul, whom I removed from before you.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned before you and doubled forever.
verses.before: Your house and your kingdom will be established forever before you; your throne will be established forever.”
verses.after: Your house and your kingdom will stand firm forever before you; your throne will be established forever.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Your house and your kingdom shall be established forever before you; your throne shall be established forever.”

verses.rationale: Keeps comprehensive transmission and vision terminology.
verses.before: According to all these words and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.
verses.after: Nathan told David all these words and the whole vision.
verses.tsw_comparator: According to all these words and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.

verses.rationale: Preserves sitting, divine address, and the house question.
verses.before: Then King David went in and sat before the LORD and said: “Who am I, Lord GOD, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
verses.after: Then King David went in and sat before the LORD. He said, “Who am I, Lord GOD, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
verses.tsw_comparator: Then King David went in and sat before the LORD and said: “Who am I, Lord GOD, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?

verses.rationale: Treats the difficult instruction-of-humanity clause as a question; note alternatives.
verses.before: And this was still a small thing in your eyes, Lord GOD, for you have spoken also concerning your servant’s house for a distant time. And this is instruction for humanity, Lord GOD.
verses.after: Even this was a small thing in your eyes, Lord GOD. You have spoken about your servant’s house far into the future. Is this the way of humankind, Lord GOD?
verses.tsw_comparator: And this was still a small thing in your eyes, Lord GOD, for you have spoken also concerning your servant’s house for a distant time. And this is instruction for humanity, Lord GOD.

verses.rationale: Retains third-person self-reference and intimate knowledge.
verses.before: What more can David say to you? You yourself know your servant, Lord GOD.
verses.after: What more can David say to you? You know your servant, Lord GOD.
verses.tsw_comparator: What more can David say to you? You yourself know your servant, Lord GOD.

verses.rationale: Keeps word and heart as the stated grounds.
verses.before: Because of your word and according to your heart you have done all this greatness, making it known to your servant.
verses.after: For the sake of your word and according to your own heart, you have done all this greatness and made it known to your servant.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because of your word and according to your heart you have done all this greatness, making it known to your servant.

verses.rationale: Preserves the communal hearing behind David’s praise.
verses.before: “Therefore you are great, Lord GOD, for there is none like you, and there is no God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
verses.after: How great you are, Lord GOD! No one is like you; there is no God besides you, as all we have heard with our own ears confirms.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Therefore you are great, Lord GOD, for there is none like you, and there is no God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

verses.rationale: Unfolds difficult pronoun shifts; retains the awkward final nations-and-gods clause.
verses.before: And who is like your people, like Israel, one nation on the earth whom God went to redeem for himself as a people, to make a name for himself and to do for you great and awe-inspiring things for your land, before your people whom you redeemed for yourself from Egypt, nations and their gods?
verses.after: Who is like your people Israel, the one nation on earth whom God went to redeem as his people and make a name for himself? You did great things for them, awesome things for your land, before your people whom you redeemed for yourself from Egypt—from nations and their gods.
verses.tsw_comparator: And who is like your people, like Israel, one nation on the earth whom God went to redeem for himself as a people, to make a name for himself and to do for you great and awe-inspiring things for your land, before your people whom you redeemed for yourself from Egypt, nations and their gods?

verses.rationale: Retains the reciprocal people-and-God formulation.
verses.before: You established your people Israel for yourself as your people forever, and you, O LORD, became their God.
verses.after: You established your people Israel as your own people forever, and you, LORD, became their God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You established your people Israel for yourself as your people forever, and you, O LORD, became their God.

verses.rationale: Keeps petition grounded in the spoken word.
verses.before: “And now, O LORD God, the word that you have spoken concerning your servant and concerning his house, establish it forever and do as you have spoken.
verses.after: Now, LORD God, establish forever the word you have spoken about your servant and his house. Do as you have said.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And now, O LORD God, the word that you have spoken concerning your servant and concerning his house, establish it forever and do as you have spoken.

verses.rationale: Connects divine name and the servant’s continuing house.
verses.before: Let your name be great forever, saying, ‘The LORD of Hosts is God over Israel,’ and let the house of your servant David be established before you.
verses.after: May your name be great forever, as people say, ‘The LORD of Armies is God over Israel.’ And may the house of your servant David stand firm before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let your name be great forever, saying, ‘The LORD of Hosts is God over Israel,’ and let the house of your servant David be established before you.

verses.rationale: Unfolds uncovering the ear and finding the heart as disclosure and courage.
verses.before: For you, O LORD of Hosts, God of Israel, have uncovered the ear of your servant, saying, ‘I will build you a house.’ Therefore your servant has found his heart to pray this prayer to you.
verses.after: LORD of Armies, God of Israel, you have revealed this to your servant: ‘I will build you a house.’ That is why your servant has found the courage to pray this prayer to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you, O LORD of Hosts, God of Israel, have uncovered the ear of your servant, saying, ‘I will build you a house.’ Therefore your servant has found his heart to pray this prayer to you.

verses.rationale: Preserves truth of words and the promised good.
verses.before: And now, Lord GOD, you are God, and your words are truth, and you have spoken this good thing to your servant.
verses.after: Now, Lord GOD, you are God, and your words are true. You have promised this good thing to your servant.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, Lord GOD, you are God, and your words are truth, and you have spoken this good thing to your servant.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated house, blessing, and forever ending.
verses.before: And now, be pleased to bless the house of your servant, so that it may continue forever before you. For you, Lord GOD, have spoken, and from your blessing the house of your servant will be blessed forever.”
verses.after: So please bless your servant’s house, that it may remain before you forever. You, Lord GOD, have spoken, and with your blessing your servant’s house will be blessed forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, be pleased to bless the house of your servant, so that it may continue forever before you. For you, Lord GOD, have spoken, and from your blessing the house of your servant will be blessed forever.”

verses.rationale: Retains uncertain named object or place rather than identifying it as Gath.
verses.before: After this David struck the Philistines and subdued them, and David took Metheg-Ammah from the hand of the Philistines.
verses.after: After this David defeated the Philistines and brought them under his rule. He took Metheg-ammah out of their hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: After this David struck the Philistines and subdued them, and David took Metheg-Ammah from the hand of the Philistines.

verses.rationale: Preserves the killing selection and unequal measures without euphemism.
verses.before: He struck Moab and measured them with a cord, making them lie down on the ground. He measured two cords to put to death and one full cord to keep alive. So the Moabites became servants to David and brought tribute.
verses.after: He also defeated Moab. He made the people lie on the ground and measured them with a cord: two cord-lengths for death and one full cord-length for life. The Moabites became David’s subjects and brought tribute.
verses.tsw_comparator: He struck Moab and measured them with a cord, making them lie down on the ground. He measured two cords to put to death and one full cord to keep alive. So the Moabites became servants to David and brought tribute.

verses.rationale: Follows read Euphrates; leaves the marching subject open.
verses.before: David struck Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, when he went to restore his power at the Euphrates River.
