verses.rationale: Supplies the likely pursued subject, retains pinned Berites, and follows read gathered without harmonizing the geography.
verses.before: Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel and Beth-Maacah and all the Berites. They gathered together and also came after him.
verses.after: Sheba passed through all Israel’s tribes to Abel and Beth-maacah, and to all the Berites. They gathered together and followed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel and Beth-Maacah and all the Berites. They gathered together and also came after him.

verses.rationale: Clarifies besiegers and preserves both ramp and wall attack.
verses.before: They came and besieged him in Abel-Beth-Maacah. They cast up a siege mound against the city, and it stood against the rampart. All the people who were with Joab were battering the wall to cause it to fall.
verses.after: Joab’s men came and besieged him in Abel-beth-maacah. They piled a siege ramp against the city, up to the outer defenses, while everyone with Joab battered the wall to bring it down.
verses.tsw_comparator: They came and besieged him in Abel-Beth-Maacah. They cast up a siege mound against the city, and it stood against the rampart. All the people who were with Joab were battering the wall to cause it to fall.

verses.rationale: Keeps the doubled appeal and the woman’s initiative.
verses.before: Then a wise woman cried out from the city, “Hear! Hear! Please say to Joab, ‘Come near here so that I may speak to you.’”
verses.after: A wise woman called from the city, “Listen! Listen! Please tell Joab, ‘Come here so I can speak to you.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then a wise woman cried out from the city, “Hear! Hear! Please say to Joab, ‘Come near here so that I may speak to you.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves the exchange establishing a hearing.
verses.before: He came near to her, and the woman said, “Are you Joab?” He said, “I am.” She said to him, “Listen to the words of your servant.” He said, “I am listening.”
verses.after: He came toward her, and she asked, “Are you Joab?” “I am,” he answered. She said, “Listen to your servant’s words.” He replied, “I am listening.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He came near to her, and the woman said, “Are you Joab?” He said, “I am.” She said to him, “Listen to the words of your servant.” He said, “I am listening.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the city’s proverbial consultation role without adding an external legal requirement.
verses.before: Then she spoke, saying, “They used to say in former times, ‘Let them surely ask counsel at Abel,’ and so they settled a matter.
verses.after: She said, “In the past people used to say, ‘Ask at Abel,’ and that would settle the matter.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then she spoke, saying, “They used to say in former times, ‘Let them surely ask counsel at Abel,’ and so they settled a matter.

verses.rationale: Preserves the mother-city and devouring images and her claim to peace.
verses.before: I am one of the peaceful and faithful in Israel. You are seeking to put to death a city and a mother in Israel. Why would you swallow up the inheritance of the LORD?”
verses.after: I am among the peaceful and faithful in Israel. You are trying to kill a city, a mother in Israel. Why would you swallow up the LORD’s inheritance?”
verses.tsw_comparator: I am one of the peaceful and faithful in Israel. You are seeking to put to death a city and a mother in Israel. Why would you swallow up the inheritance of the LORD?”

verses.rationale: Retains the doubled denial as Joab’s speech, in tension with the siege.
verses.before: Joab answered and said, “Far be it, far be it from me that I should swallow up or destroy!
verses.after: Joab answered, “Far be it from me—far be it! I would never swallow up or destroy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joab answered and said, “Far be it, far be it from me that I should swallow up or destroy!

verses.rationale: Keeps the single-person demand and the woman’s explicit promised beheading.
verses.before: The matter is not so. But a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba son of Bichri by name, has lifted his hand against the king, against David. Give him alone, and I will go away from the city.” The woman said to Joab, “Look, his head will be thrown to you over the wall.”
verses.after: That is not the matter. A man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba son of Bichri, has raised his hand against King David. Hand over that man alone, and I will withdraw from the city.” The woman told Joab, “His head will be thrown to you over the wall.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The matter is not so. But a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba son of Bichri by name, has lifted his hand against the king, against David. Give him alone, and I will go away from the city.” The woman said to Joab, “Look, his head will be thrown to you over the wall.”

verses.rationale: Retains her effective counsel, the killing, signal, and dispersal without turning it into a bloodless rescue.
verses.before: Then the woman came to all the people in her wisdom. They cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it out to Joab. He blew the ram’s horn, and they dispersed from the city, each to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.
verses.after: The woman went to all the people with her wise counsel. They cut off Sheba son of Bichri’s head and threw it to Joab. He blew the ram’s horn, and the men scattered from the city, each to his own tent. Joab returned to the king in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the woman came to all the people in her wisdom. They cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it out to Joab. He blew the ram’s horn, and they dispersed from the city, each to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.

verses.rationale: Follows read Cherethites and keeps Joab’s restored command explicit.
verses.before: Joab was over all the army of Israel; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites;
verses.after: Joab was over Israel’s whole army. Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joab was over all the army of Israel; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites;

verses.rationale: Names coerced labor and distinguishes the administrative offices.
verses.before: Adoram was over forced labor; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;
verses.after: Adoram was over the forced labor, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder.
verses.tsw_comparator: Adoram was over forced labor; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;

verses.rationale: Follows read Sheva while retaining both priests.
verses.before: Sheva was scribe; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
verses.after: Sheva was the scribe, and Zadok and Abiathar were priests.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sheva was scribe; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;

verses.rationale: Preserves priest rather than replacing the term with chief minister.
verses.before: and Ira the Jairite also was priest to David.
verses.after: Ira the Jairite was also a priest for David.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Ira the Jairite also was priest to David.

verses.rationale: Retains duration, seeking the face, and the divine attribution without making the next proposed remedy a divine command.
verses.before: There was a famine in the days of David for three years, year after year. David sought the face of the LORD, and the LORD said, “There is bloodguilt upon Saul and upon his house because he put the Gibeonites to death.”
verses.after: In David’s days there was a famine for three years, year after year. David sought the LORD’s face, and the LORD said, “It is because of Saul and his bloodstained house, because he put the Gibeonites to death.”
verses.tsw_comparator: There was a famine in the days of David for three years, year after year. David sought the face of the LORD, and the LORD said, “There is bloodguilt upon Saul and upon his house because he put the Gibeonites to death.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the background oath, ethnicity, and destructive zeal.
verses.before: So the king called the Gibeonites and spoke to them. Now the Gibeonites were not from the children of Israel but from the remnant of the Amorites. The children of Israel had sworn to them, but Saul had sought to strike them in his zeal for the children of Israel and Judah.
verses.after: The king summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them. The Gibeonites were not Israelites but a remnant of the Amorites. The Israelites had sworn an oath to them, yet Saul had sought to strike them down in his zeal for Israel and Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the king called the Gibeonites and spoke to them. Now the Gibeonites were not from the children of Israel but from the remnant of the Amorites. The children of Israel had sworn to them, but Saul had sought to strike them in his zeal for the children of Israel and Judah.

verses.rationale: Keeps atonement and inheritance as biblical terms within David’s question.
verses.before: David said to the Gibeonites, “What will I do for you? And how will I make atonement, so that you may bless the inheritance of the LORD?”
verses.after: David asked the Gibeonites, “What shall I do for you? How can I make atonement, so that you will bless the LORD’s inheritance?”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to the Gibeonites, “What shall I do for you? And how shall I make atonement, so that you may bless the inheritance of the LORD?”

verses.rationale: Follows read our and clarifies lack of authority while retaining David’s open promise.
verses.before: The Gibeonites said to him, “It is not a matter of silver or gold for us with Saul or with his house, and it is not for us to put any man in Israel to death.” He said, “Whatever you say, I will do for you.”
verses.after: The Gibeonites answered, “Our dispute with Saul and his house is not about silver or gold, and we have no right to put anyone in Israel to death.” He said, “Tell me what you want, and I will do it for you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The Gibeonites said to him, “It is not a matter of silver or gold for us with Saul or with his house, and it is not for us to put any man in Israel to death.” He said, “Whatever you say, I will do for you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the intended eradication as the victims’ account.
verses.before: They said to the king, “The man who consumed us and who planned to destroy us, so that we would have no place in all the territory of Israel—
verses.after: They told the king, “The man who consumed us and plotted against us would have destroyed us, leaving us no place anywhere in Israel’s territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to the king, “The man who consumed us and who planned to destroy us, so that we would have no place in all the territory of Israel—

verses.rationale: Keeps seven males, lethal public exposure, chosen designation, and David’s assent; the exact execution method remains uncertain.
verses.before: let seven men from his sons be given to us, and we will hang them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the LORD.” The king said, “I will give them.”
verses.after: Let seven of his male descendants be handed over to us. We will expose them in death before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the LORD’s chosen one.” The king said, “I will hand them over.”
verses.tsw_comparator: let seven men from his sons be given to us, and we will hang them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the LORD.” The king said, “I will give them.”

verses.rationale: Retains the distinct oath and full relationship of the spared man.
verses.before: But the king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, son of Saul, because of the oath of the LORD that was between them, between David and Jonathan son of Saul.
verses.after: But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Saul’s son Jonathan, because of the oath before the LORD between David and Jonathan son of Saul.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, son of Saul, because of the oath of the LORD that was between them, between David and Jonathan son of Saul.

verses.rationale: Preserves pinned Michal and borne rather than silently replacing either to reconcile other passages.
verses.before: The king took the two sons of Rizpah daughter of Aiah whom she had borne to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth, and the five sons of Merab daughter of Saul whom she had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.
verses.after: The king took Armoni and Mephibosheth, the two sons whom Rizpah daughter of Aiah had borne to Saul, and the five sons whom Saul’s daughter Michal had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king took the two sons of Rizpah daughter of Aiah whom she had borne to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth, and the five sons of Merab daughter of Saul whom she had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.

verses.rationale: Follows all three read forms and retains deaths, place, and harvest timing.
verses.before: He gave them into the hand of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them on the mountain before the LORD, and the seven fell together. They were put to death in the first days of harvest, at the beginning of barley harvest.
verses.after: He handed them over to the Gibeonites, who exposed them in death on the hill before the LORD. All seven fell together. They were put to death in the first days of harvest, at the beginning of the barley harvest.
verses.tsw_comparator: He gave them into the hand of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them on the mountain before the LORD, and the seven fell together. They were put to death in the first days of harvest, at the beginning of barley harvest.

verses.rationale: Preserves her sustained guarding, both kinds of scavenger, and the rainfall endpoint without inventing a duration.
verses.before: Rizpah daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it for herself upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water was poured upon them from the heavens. She did not allow the birds of the heavens to rest upon them by day or the animals of the field by night.
verses.after: Rizpah daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it for herself on the rock. From the beginning of harvest until water poured down on them from the sky, she allowed no bird of the sky to settle on them by day, and no wild animal by night.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rizpah daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it for herself upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water was poured upon them from the heavens. She did not allow the birds of the heavens to rest upon them by day or the animals of the field by night.

verses.rationale: Keeps her action as the stated prompt for David’s response.
verses.before: It was told to David what Rizpah daughter of Aiah, concubine of Saul, had done.
verses.after: David was told what Rizpah daughter of Aiah, Saul’s concubine, had done.
verses.tsw_comparator: It was told to David what Rizpah daughter of Aiah, concubine of Saul, had done.

verses.rationale: Preserves this account’s public-square location and follows the read forms without harmonizing 1 Samuel’s wall wording.
verses.before: David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the citizens of Jabesh-Gilead, who had stolen them from the public square of Beth-Shan, where the Philistines had hung them on the day the Philistines struck Saul at Gilboa.
verses.after: David went and retrieved the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from the people of Jabesh-gilead. They had secretly taken them from the public square of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hung them on the day they struck Saul down on Gilboa.
verses.tsw_comparator: David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the citizens of Jabesh-Gilead, who had stolen them from the public square of Beth-Shan, where the Philistines had hung them on the day the Philistines struck Saul at Gilboa.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two groups of remains distinct.
verses.before: He brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son, and they gathered the bones of people who had been hanged.
verses.after: He brought up the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from there, and they gathered the bones of those who had been exposed in death.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son, and they gathered the bones of those who had been hanged.

verses.rationale: Retains burial details and the narrative’s after-this sequence without claiming execution alone ended the famine.
verses.before: They buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the land of Benjamin at Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father. They did all that the king commanded. And after that God was entreated for the land.
verses.after: They buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan at Zela in Benjamin, in the tomb of Saul’s father Kish. They did everything the king commanded. After this, God responded to pleas for the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: They buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the land of Benjamin at Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father. They did all that the king commanded. And after that God was entreated for the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves renewed conflict and the king’s vulnerability.
verses.before: There was again war between the Philistines and Israel. David went down, and his servants with him, and they fought the Philistines. David became weary.
verses.after: Once again there was war between the Philistines and Israel. David went down with his servants to fight the Philistines, and David grew weary.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was again war between the Philistines and Israel. David went down, and his servants with him, and they fought the Philistines. David became weary.

verses.rationale: Follows read Ishbi, keeps the weight, and does not specify the unstated kind of new weapon.
verses.before: Ishbi-Benob, who was among the descendants of the giant, whose spear weighed three hundred shekels of bronze and who was girded with a new weapon, thought to strike David.
verses.after: Ishbi-benob, one of Rapha’s descendants, had a bronze spearhead weighing three hundred shekels and was armed with a new weapon. He intended to strike David down.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ishbi-Benob, who was among the descendants of the giant, whose spear weighed three hundred shekels of bronze and who was girded with a new weapon, thought to strike David.

verses.rationale: Retains Abishai’s rescue and the lamp image behind the ban.
verses.before: Yet Abishai son of Zeruiah came to his aid and struck the Philistine and put him to death. Then the men of David swore to him, saying, “You will not go out with us to battle again, so that you do not extinguish the lamp of Israel.”
verses.after: But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to his aid, struck the Philistine, and killed him. Then David’s men swore to him, “You must never go into battle with us again, or you may extinguish Israel’s lamp.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to his aid and struck the Philistine and put him to death. Then the men of David swore to him, saying, “You shall not go out with us to battle again, so that you do not extinguish the lamp of Israel.”

verses.rationale: Keeps pinned Gob, Sibbecai, and Saph without replacing them from a parallel account.
verses.before: After this there was again battle with the Philistines at Gob. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite struck Saph, who was among the descendants of the giant.
verses.after: After this, there was another battle with the Philistines at Gob. There Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph, one of Rapha’s descendants.
verses.tsw_comparator: After this there was again battle with the Philistines at Gob. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite struck Saph, who was among the descendants of the giant.

verses.rationale: Retains the consequential pinned Elhanan-Goliath reading without adding brother of.
verses.before: There was again battle with the Philistines at Gob, and Elhanan son of Jaare-Oregim the Bethlehemite struck Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
verses.after: In another battle with the Philistines at Gob, Elhanan son of Jaare-oregim the Bethlehemite struck down Goliath the Gittite. Goliath’s spear shaft was like a weaver’s beam.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was again battle with the Philistines at Gob, and Elhanan son of Jaare-Oregim the Bethlehemite struck Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.

verses.rationale: Follows read size and preserves the complete six-and-six count.
verses.before: There was again battle at Gath, where there was a man of great stature who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in number. He also was descended from the giant.
verses.after: There was another battle at Gath. A man of great size was there, with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot—twenty-four in all. He too was descended from Rapha.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was again battle at Gath, where there was a man of great stature who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in number. He also was descended from the giant.

verses.rationale: Follows read Shimeah and keeps this Jonathan distinct from Saul’s son.
verses.before: He taunted Israel, and Jonathan son of Shimei, David’s brother, struck him.
verses.after: When he taunted Israel, Jonathan, the son of David’s brother Shimeah, struck him down.
verses.tsw_comparator: He taunted Israel, and Jonathan son of Shimei, David’s brother, struck him.

verses.rationale: Retains the four-person summary and collective attribution without erasing the named killers.
verses.before: These four were descended from the giant in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.
verses.after: These four were descended from Rapha in Gath. They fell by the hands of David and his servants.
verses.tsw_comparator: These four were descended from the giant in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

verses.rationale: Keeps the narrative frame and separate mention of Saul.
verses.before: David spoke to the LORD the words of this song on the day the LORD rescued him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
verses.after: David spoke the words of this song to the LORD when the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from Saul’s hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: David spoke to the LORD the words of this song on the day the LORD rescued him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.

verses.rationale: Preserves three protective images and starts the sustained poem inside verse formatting.
verses.before: He said: The LORD is my rock, my stronghold, and my rescuer.
verses.after: He said: “The LORD is my cliff, my fortress, and the one who delivers me.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said: The LORD is my rock, my stronghold, and my rescuer.

verses.rationale: Keeps horn and all refuge images, including the turn to direct address.
verses.before: My God is my rock; in him I take refuge— my shield, the horn of my salvation, my high fortress and my refuge, my savior; you save me from violence.
verses.after: My God is my rock; in him I take refuge, my shield and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold and my place of escape. My savior, you save me from violence.
verses.tsw_comparator: My God is my rock; in him I take refuge— my shield, the horn of my salvation, my high fortress and my refuge, my savior; you save me from violence.

verses.rationale: Retains the call-and-rescue relationship without importing a line from Psalm 18.
verses.before: I call upon the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and I am saved from my enemies.
verses.after: I call to the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and I am saved from my enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: I call upon the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and I am saved from my enemies.

verses.rationale: Keeps Samuel’s breakers rather than the parallel psalm’s cords at this point.
verses.before: For the waves of death surrounded me; torrents of destruction terrified me.
verses.after: The breakers of death surrounded me; torrents of destruction terrified me.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the waves of death surrounded me; torrents of destruction terrified me.

verses.rationale: Retains Sheol and the distinct cords and traps.
verses.before: The cords of Sheol surrounded me; the snares of death confronted me.
verses.after: The cords of Sheol coiled around me; the snares of death confronted me.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cords of Sheol surrounded me; the snares of death confronted me.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated calling, temple, and embodied hearing.
verses.before: In my distress I called upon the LORD, and to my God I called. From his temple he heard my voice, and my cry came into his ears.
verses.after: In my distress I called to the LORD; to my God I called. From his temple he heard my voice; my cry for help reached his ears.
verses.tsw_comparator: In my distress I called upon the LORD, and to my God I called. From his temple he heard my voice, and my cry came into his ears.

verses.rationale: Follows read shaking and retains foundations of heaven rather than mountains from the parallel psalm.
verses.before: Then the earth shook and trembled; the foundations of the heavens quaked and shook because he was angry.
verses.after: Then the earth shook and quaked; the foundations of heaven trembled. They shook because he was angry.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the earth shook and trembled; the foundations of the heavens quaked and shook because he was angry.

verses.rationale: Preserves the full anthropomorphic storm-fire imagery.
verses.before: Smoke rose from his nostrils, and consuming fire from his mouth; coals burned from it.
verses.after: Smoke rose from his nostrils; devouring fire came from his mouth. Burning coals blazed from him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Smoke rose from his nostrils, and consuming fire from his mouth; coals burned from it.

verses.rationale: Keeps descent and darkness as spatial poetry.
verses.before: He bent the heavens and came down, and thick darkness was under his feet.
verses.after: He bent the heavens and came down, thick darkness beneath his feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: He bent the heavens and came down, and thick darkness was under his feet.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned appeared rather than importing soared from Psalm 18.
verses.before: He rode upon a cherub and flew; he was seen upon the wings of the wind.
verses.after: He rode a cherub and flew; he appeared on the wings of the wind.
verses.tsw_comparator: He rode upon a cherub and flew; he was seen upon the wings of the wind.

verses.rationale: Preserves plural shelters and the difficult gathered-water image.
verses.before: He made darkness booths around him, a gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies.
verses.after: He made darkness shelters around him, piled-up waters, thick clouds of the skies.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made darkness booths around him, a gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies.

verses.rationale: Keeps Samuel’s short line without adding hail from a parallel.
verses.before: From the brightness before him coals of fire burned.
verses.after: From the brightness before him burning coals blazed.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the brightness before him coals of fire burned.

verses.rationale: Retains the voice-thunder parallel and divine title.
verses.before: The LORD thundered from the heavens, and the Most High gave his voice.
verses.after: The LORD thundered from heaven; the Most High gave his voice.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD thundered from the heavens, and the Most High gave his voice.

verses.rationale: Follows the read verb while retaining the implied targets and lightning parallel.
verses.before: He sent arrows and scattered them, lightning and confused them.
verses.after: He sent arrows and scattered them, lightning, and threw them into confusion.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sent arrows and scattered them, lightning and confused them.

verses.rationale: Keeps sea channels, exposed foundations, and the doubled rebuke-breath agency.
verses.before: Then the channels of the sea appeared; the foundations of the world were uncovered at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.
verses.after: The channels of the sea appeared; the world’s foundations lay bare at the LORD’s rebuke, at the blast of breath from his nostrils.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the channels of the sea appeared; the foundations of the world were uncovered at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.

verses.rationale: Preserves rescue as drawing out of waters, not a generalized trouble metaphor.
verses.before: He sent from on high; he took me. He drew me out of great waters.
verses.after: He reached down from on high and took me; he drew me out of many waters.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sent from on high; he took me. He drew me out of great waters.

verses.rationale: Keeps the singular enemy and plural haters.
verses.before: He rescued me from my strong enemy, from people who hated me, for they were too mighty for me.
verses.after: He rescued me from my strong enemy, from those who hated me, for they were stronger than I.
verses.tsw_comparator: He rescued me from my strong enemy, from those who hated me, for they were too mighty for me.

verses.rationale: Retains the day of vulnerability and contrasting support.
verses.before: They confronted me on the day of my disaster, but the LORD was my support.
verses.after: They confronted me on my day of disaster, but the LORD became my support.
verses.tsw_comparator: They confronted me on the day of my disaster, but the LORD was my support.

verses.rationale: Keeps the roomy-place image and stated delight.
verses.before: He brought me out into a broad place; he rescued me because he delighted in me.
verses.after: He brought me out into a spacious place; he rescued me because he delighted in me.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought me out into a broad place; he rescued me because he delighted in me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the speaker’s claim and embodied clean hands without harmonizing the narrative’s moral tensions.
verses.before: The LORD dealt with me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands he returned to me.
verses.after: The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness; he repaid me according to the cleanness of my hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD dealt with me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands he returned to me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the claimed fidelity as David’s sung words.
verses.before: For I have kept the ways of the LORD and have not acted wickedly away from my God.
verses.after: For I have kept the LORD’s ways and have not wickedly turned from my God.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I have kept the ways of the LORD and have not acted wickedly away from my God.

verses.rationale: Follows read plural judgments and retains both law terms.
verses.before: For all his judgments were before me, and as for his statutes, I did not turn away from them.
verses.after: All his judgments are before me; I do not turn aside from his statutes.
verses.tsw_comparator: For all his judgments were before me, and as for his statutes, I did not turn away from them.

verses.rationale: Keeps blameless and personal guilt rather than weakening either claim.
verses.before: I was blameless toward him, and I guarded myself from my guilt.
verses.after: I have been blameless before him and have guarded myself from my own guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: I was blameless toward him, and I guarded myself from my guilt.

verses.rationale: Preserves the refrain’s variation: this verse does not repeat hands.
verses.before: So the LORD returned to me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness before his eyes.
verses.after: The LORD repaid me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness before his eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the LORD returned to me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness before his eyes.

verses.rationale: Retains the reciprocal word pattern and Samuel’s warrior wording.
verses.before: With the faithful you show yourself faithful; with the blameless mighty one you show yourself blameless.
verses.after: With the faithful you show yourself faithful; with the blameless warrior you show yourself blameless.
verses.tsw_comparator: With the faithful you show yourself faithful; with the blameless mighty one you show yourself blameless.

verses.rationale: Keeps contrasting responses without flattening the difficult second verb into simple opposition.
verses.before: With the pure you show yourself pure, but with the twisted you show yourself shrewd.
verses.after: With the pure you show yourself pure; with the crooked you show yourself shrewd.
verses.tsw_comparator: With the pure you show yourself pure, but with the twisted you show yourself shrewd.

verses.rationale: Preserves the social contrast and watching eyes.
verses.before: You save an afflicted people, but your eyes are upon the proud to bring them low.
verses.after: You save an afflicted people, but your eyes are on the proud to bring them low.
verses.tsw_comparator: You save an afflicted people, but your eyes are upon the proud to bring them low.

verses.rationale: Keeps you are my lamp rather than harmonizing the parallel psalm’s lighting a lamp.
verses.before: For you are my lamp, O LORD, and the LORD illumines my darkness.
verses.after: For you are my lamp, LORD; the LORD lights up my darkness.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you are my lamp, O LORD, and the LORD illumines my darkness.

verses.rationale: Retains military imagery and balanced with-you/with-God clauses.
verses.before: For by you I run against a troop; by my God I leap over a wall.
verses.after: With you I can charge a raiding band; with my God I can leap a wall.
verses.tsw_comparator: For by you I run against a troop; by my God I leap over a wall.

verses.rationale: Preserves complete way, metal-testing image, and refuge refrain.
verses.before: As for God, his way is blameless. The word of the LORD is refined. He is a shield to everyone who take refuge in him.
verses.after: God’s way is complete; the LORD’s word is refined. He is a shield to all who take refuge in him.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for God, his way is blameless. The word of the LORD is refined. He is a shield to all who take refuge in him.

verses.rationale: Keeps both rhetorical questions and the rock image.
verses.before: For who is God besides the LORD? And who is a rock besides our God?
verses.after: Who is God apart from the LORD? Who is a rock apart from our God?
verses.tsw_comparator: For who is God besides the LORD? And who is a rock besides our God?

verses.rationale: Follows read my way and renders the difficult loosening verb without borrowing the parallel psalm’s girding line.
verses.before: God is my strong fortress, and he makes my way blameless.
verses.after: God is my strong refuge; he clears my way completely.
verses.tsw_comparator: God is my strong fortress, and he makes my way blameless.

verses.rationale: Follows read my feet and retains the female deer comparison and high places.
verses.before: He makes my feet like the feet of deer and makes me stand upon my heights.
verses.after: He makes my feet like a doe’s and sets me on my heights.
verses.tsw_comparator: He makes my feet like the feet of deer and makes me stand upon my heights.

verses.rationale: Keeps training, body parts, and the ancient bronze-bow image.
verses.before: He trains my hands for battle, so that my arms bend a bow of bronze.
verses.after: He trains my hands for war, so my arms can bend a bronze bow.
verses.tsw_comparator: He trains my hands for battle, so that my arms bend a bow of bronze.

verses.rationale: Retains a defensible answering sense of the difficult noun rather than silently substituting Psalm 18’s form.
verses.before: You have given me the shield of your salvation, and your answering care has made me great.
verses.after: You give me the shield of your salvation; your answering me makes me great.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have given me the shield of your salvation, and your answering care has made me great.

verses.rationale: Preserves spacious footing and anatomical ankles.
verses.before: You make a broad place for my steps beneath me, and my ankles do not slip.
verses.after: You give my steps room beneath me, and my ankles do not give way.
verses.tsw_comparator: You make a broad place for my steps beneath me, and my ankles do not slip.

verses.rationale: Keeps the violence and relentless pursuit in the song’s own voice.
verses.before: I pursued my enemies and destroyed them, and I did not turn back until they were consumed.
verses.after: I pursue my enemies and destroy them; I do not turn back until I finish them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I pursued my enemies and destroyed them, and I did not turn back until they were consumed.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated finishing and the enemies underfoot.
verses.before: I consumed them and shattered them so that they did not rise; they fell under my feet.
verses.after: I finish them and crush them; they cannot rise. They fall beneath my feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: I consumed them and shattered them so that they did not rise; they fell under my feet.

verses.rationale: Keeps girding and forced subjection rather than abstracting the victory.
verses.before: You girded me with strength for battle; you made people who rose against me bow beneath me.
verses.after: You gird me with strength for battle; you make those who rise against me bow beneath me.
verses.tsw_comparator: You girded me with strength for battle; you made those who rose against me bow beneath me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the backs image of flight and explicit destruction.
verses.before: You made my enemies turn their backs to me, and people who hated me I destroyed.
verses.after: You give me my enemies’ backs; I wipe out those who hate me.
verses.tsw_comparator: You made my enemies turn their backs to me, and those who hated me I destroyed.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned looking rather than changing it to crying out from the parallel psalm.
verses.before: They looked, but there was no one to save; to the LORD, but he did not answer them.
verses.after: They look for help, but no one saves; they look to the LORD, but he does not answer.
verses.tsw_comparator: They looked, but there was no one to save; to the LORD, but he did not answer them.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three violent actions and both material comparisons.
verses.before: I beat them fine like the dust of the earth; like mud of the streets I crushed them and stamped them down.
verses.after: I grind them like the dust of the earth; like mud in the streets, I crush and trample them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I beat them fine like the dust of the earth; like mud of the streets I crushed them and stamped them down.

verses.rationale: Retains my people and the move from domestic conflict to foreign rule.
verses.before: You rescued me from the disputes of my people; you kept me as head of nations. A people I had not known served me.
verses.after: You deliver me from my people’s disputes; you preserve me as head of nations. A people I did not know serves me.
verses.tsw_comparator: You rescued me from the disputes of my people; you kept me as head of nations. A people I had not known served me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the compelled or feigned submission sense and immediate hearing.
verses.before: Foreigners came cringing to me; as soon as their ear heard, they obeyed me.
verses.after: Foreigners cringe before me; at the mere hearing of me they obey.
verses.tsw_comparator: Foreigners came cringing to me; as soon as their ear heard, they obeyed me.

verses.rationale: Uses the possible faltering sense of the difficult verb; its relation to girding requires a note.
verses.before: Foreigners faded and came trembling from their strongholds.
verses.after: Foreigners lose heart and come limping from their strongholds.
verses.tsw_comparator: Foreigners faded and came trembling from their strongholds.

verses.rationale: Preserves the doubled rock and acclamations.
verses.before: The LORD lives! Blessed be my rock! Exalted be God, the rock of my salvation—
verses.after: The LORD lives! Blessed be my rock! Exalted be God, the rock of my salvation!
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD lives! Blessed be my rock! Exalted be God, the rock of my salvation—

verses.rationale: Keeps vengeance and political subjection explicit; the sentence continues.
verses.before: the God who gives vengeance for me and brings peoples down beneath me,
verses.after: He is the God who gives me vengeance, who brings peoples down beneath me,
verses.tsw_comparator: the God who gives vengeance for me and brings peoples down beneath me,

verses.rationale: Preserves the switch from third-person praise to second-person address.
verses.before: who brings me out from my enemies. You exalted me above people who rose against me; from the man of violence you rescued me.
verses.after: who brings me out from my enemies. You lift me above those who rise against me; you rescue me from violent men.
verses.tsw_comparator: who brings me out from my enemies. You exalted me above those who rose against me; from the man of violence you rescued me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the nations as the setting for thanksgiving and the name theme.
verses.before: So I will give thanks to you, O LORD, among the nations, and to your name I will sing.
verses.after: So I will thank you among the nations, LORD, and sing praise to your name.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I will give thanks to you, O LORD, among the nations, and to your name I will sing.

verses.rationale: Follows read tower rather than written magnifies victories, preserving anointed, offspring, and enduring love.
verses.before: He is a tower of salvation for his king and shows steadfast love to his anointed, to David and to his offspring forever.
verses.after: He is a tower of salvation for his king, showing steadfast love to his anointed, to David and his offspring forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He is a tower of salvation for his king and shows steadfast love to his anointed, to David and to his offspring forever.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated declaration and the layered descriptions without turning last words into an exact deathbed chronology.
verses.before: These are the last words of David: The declaration of David son of Jesse, the declaration of the man raised on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the pleasant singer of Israel’s songs.
verses.after: These are David’s last words: “The declaration of David son of Jesse, the declaration of the man raised on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, the sweet singer of Israel’s songs:
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the last words of David: The declaration of David son of Jesse, the declaration of the man raised on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the pleasant singer of Israel’s songs.

verses.rationale: Keeps Spirit, mediated speech, and tongue image.
verses.before: The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me, and his word was upon my tongue.
verses.after: The Spirit of the LORD has spoken through me; his word is on my tongue.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me, and his word was upon my tongue.

verses.rationale: Preserves parallel divine titles and the ruler’s justice and fear of God.
verses.before: The God of Israel spoke; the Rock of Israel said to me: “One who rules humanity righteously, who rules in the fear of God,
verses.after: The God of Israel has spoken; the Rock of Israel has said to me: ‘One who rules people justly, who rules in the fear of God,
verses.tsw_comparator: The God of Israel spoke; the Rock of Israel said to me: “One who rules humanity righteously, who rules in the fear of God,

verses.rationale: Unfolds the compressed light-rain-growth image with its implied comparison.
verses.before: is like the light of morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds, when from brightness after rain grass springs from the earth.”
verses.after: is like morning light when the sun rises, a morning without clouds, like brightness after rain that brings grass from the earth.’
verses.tsw_comparator: is like the light of morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds, when from brightness after rain grass springs from the earth.”

verses.rationale: Reads the two negative clauses as rhetorical questions while noting the alternative declarative reading.
verses.before: For is not my house so with God? For he has made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in everything and secure. Will he not cause to sprout all my salvation and all my desire?
verses.after: Is not my house like this with God? He has made an everlasting covenant with me, ordered in every part and secure. Will he not make all my salvation and all my desire spring up?
verses.tsw_comparator: For is not my house so with God? For he has made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in everything and secure. Will he not cause to sprout all my salvation and all my desire?

verses.rationale: Keeps the thorns image and warning against barehanded contact.
verses.before: But worthless men are all like thorns thrown away, for they cannot be taken with the hand.
verses.after: But the worthless are all like thorns thrown aside; they cannot be taken with the hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: But worthless men are all like thorns thrown away, for they cannot be taken with the hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves protective implements and the difficult final place expression without importing a named location.
verses.before: The man who touches them must arm himself with iron and the shaft of a spear, and they are utterly burned with fire where they lie.
verses.after: Whoever touches them must be armed with iron and a spear shaft. They will be completely burned with fire where they lie.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The man who touches them must arm himself with iron and the shaft of a spear, and they are utterly burned with fire where they lie.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult pinned names and eight hundred rather than replacing them from the parallel list.
verses.before: These are the names of David’s mighty men: Josheb-Basshebeth the Tahchemonite, chief of the Three. He wielded his spear against eight hundred whom he killed at one time.
verses.after: These are the names of David’s warriors: Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite, chief of the Three. He was Adino the Eznite, who struck down eight hundred at one time.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the names of David’s mighty men: Josheb-Basshebeth the Tahchemonite, chief of the Three. He wielded his spear against eight hundred whom he killed at one time.

verses.rationale: Follows read Dodo and warriors, retains both son relationships, and continues into Eleazar’s stand.
verses.before: After him was Eleazar son of Dodo, son of Ahohi, among the three mighty men with David when they defied the Philistines who were gathered there for battle and the men of Israel withdrew.
verses.after: After him was Eleazar son of Dodo, son of Ahohi, one of the three warriors with David when they taunted the Philistines gathered there for battle. The men of Israel withdrew,
verses.tsw_comparator: After him was Eleazar son of Dodo, son of Ahohi, among the three mighty men with David when they defied the Philistines who were gathered there for battle and the men of Israel withdrew.

verses.rationale: Keeps exhausted hand, divine victory, and the others’ limited return.
verses.before: He arose and struck the Philistines until his hand grew weary and his hand clung to the sword. The LORD brought about a great victory that day, and the people returned after him only to strip the slain.
verses.after: but he stood his ground and struck the Philistines until his hand grew weary and clung to the sword. The LORD brought about a great victory that day. The people returned after him only to strip the dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: He arose and struck the Philistines until his hand grew weary and his hand clung to the sword. The LORD brought about a great victory that day, and the people returned after him only to strip the slain.

verses.rationale: Retains lentils and the uncertain gathering expression as a troop, not an invented place name.
verses.before: After him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines gathered at Lehi, where there was a plot of ground full of lentils, and the people fled before the Philistines.
verses.after: After him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines gathered in a band where there was a field full of lentils, and the people fled before them.
verses.tsw_comparator: After him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines gathered at Lehi, where there was a plot of ground full of lentils, and the people fled before the Philistines.

verses.rationale: Keeps the field defense and repeats the same victory formula as verse 10.
verses.before: But he stationed himself among the plot, rescued it, and struck the Philistines. The LORD brought about a great victory.
verses.after: But he stood in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines. The LORD brought about a great victory.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he stationed himself in the midst of the plot, rescued it, and struck the Philistines. The LORD brought about a great victory.

verses.rationale: Follows read three rather than written thirty and preserves both locations.
verses.before: Three of the thirty leaders went down and came to David at harvest time to the cave of Adullam, while a troop of Philistines was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.after: At harvest time, three of the thirty chiefs went down to David at the cave of Adullam, while a Philistine band was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.tsw_comparator: Three of the thirty leaders went down and came to David at harvest time to the cave of Adullam, while a troop of Philistines was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.

verses.rationale: Keeps the simultaneous positions that explain the danger.
verses.before: David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then in Bethlehem.
verses.after: David was in the stronghold then, and a Philistine garrison was in Bethlehem.
verses.tsw_comparator: David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then in Bethlehem.

verses.rationale: Preserves a wish rather than converting it into an explicit order.
verses.before: David longed and said, “Who would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate?”
verses.after: David voiced a longing: “If only someone would give me water from the well beside Bethlehem’s gate!”
verses.tsw_comparator: David longed and said, “Who would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the dangerous action, repeated well, refusal, and libation.
verses.before: Then the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Philistines, drew water from the well of Bethlehem that was by the gate, carried it, and brought it to David. But he was not willing to drink it; he poured it out to the LORD.
verses.after: The three warriors broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well beside Bethlehem’s gate, and carried it back to David. But he refused to drink it and poured it out to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Philistines, drew water from the well of Bethlehem that was by the gate, carried it, and brought it to David. But he was not willing to drink it; he poured it out to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the elliptical blood question without turning the water into literal blood.
verses.before: He said, “Far be it from me, O LORD, that I should do this! Is this not the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?” So he was not willing to drink it. These things the three mighty men did.
verses.after: He said, “LORD, far be it from me to do this! Is this not the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?” He would not drink it. These were the deeds of the three warriors.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Far be it from me, O LORD, that I should do this! Is this not the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?” So he was not willing to drink it. These things the three mighty men did.

verses.rationale: Follows read Three and retains the number and group designation despite its difficulty with the next verse.
verses.before: Abishai brother of Joab, son of Zeruiah, was chief of the Thirty. He wielded his spear against three hundred and killed them and had a name among the Three.
verses.after: Abishai, Joab’s brother and a son of Zeruiah, was chief of the Three. He raised his spear against three hundred and killed them, winning a name among the Three.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abishai brother of Joab, son of Zeruiah, was chief of the Thirty. He wielded his spear against three hundred and killed them and had a name among the Three.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unresolved repeated group name rather than silently substituting Thirty.
verses.before: Was he not the most honored of the Thirty? He became their commander, but he did not attain to the Three.
verses.after: He was the most honored of the Three and became their commander, but he did not attain the rank of the Three.
verses.tsw_comparator: Was he not the most honored of the Thirty? He became their commander, but he did not attain to the Three.

verses.rationale: Follows read valiant and lion; retains the uncertain ariels term with explanation in Vocabulary.
verses.before: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the son of a valiant man from Kabzeel, great in deeds. He struck the two sons of Ariel of Moab. He also went down and struck a lion among a pit on a snowy day.
verses.after: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the son of a valiant man from Kabzeel, a man of many deeds. He struck down Moab’s two ariels. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.
verses.tsw_comparator: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the son of a valiant man from Kabzeel, great in deeds. He struck the two sons of Ariel of Moab. He also went down and struck a lion in the midst of a pit on a snowy day.

verses.rationale: Follows read man of appearance and preserves the reversal of weapons.
verses.before: He struck an Egyptian, an impressive man. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand, but Benaiah went down to him with a staff, snatched the spear from the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.
verses.after: He also struck down an imposing Egyptian. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand, but Benaiah went against him with a staff, seized the spear from his hand, and killed him with his own spear.
verses.tsw_comparator: He struck an Egyptian, an impressive man. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand, but Benaiah went down to him with a staff, snatched the spear from the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.

verses.rationale: Keeps the summary honor without asserting membership beyond the source.
verses.before: These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did and had a name among the three mighty men.
verses.after: Benaiah son of Jehoiada did these things and won a name among the three warriors.
verses.tsw_comparator: These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did and had a name among the three mighty men.

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit Thirty/Three distinction and the likely guard office.
verses.before: He was more honored than the Thirty, but he did not attain to the Three. David set him over his guard.
verses.after: He was more honored than the Thirty, though he did not attain the rank of the Three. David put him over his personal guard.
verses.tsw_comparator: He was more honored than the Thirty, but he did not attain to the Three. David set him over his guard.

verses.rationale: Begins the roster and retains both relationships without imposing an artificial total.
verses.before: Asahel brother of Joab was among the Thirty; Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem;
verses.after: Among the Thirty were Asahel, Joab’s brother; Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem;
verses.tsw_comparator: Asahel brother of Joab was among the Thirty; Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem;

verses.after: Zalmon the Ahohite; Maharai the Netophathite;

verses.after: Abi-albon the Arbathite; Azmaveth the Barhumite;

verses.rationale: Keeps the source’s differing Hararite and Ararite forms.

verses.after: Shammah the Hararite; Ahiam son of Sharar the Ararite;

verses.before: Eliphelet son of Ahasbai, son of the Maacathite; Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite;
verses.after: Eliphelet son of Ahasbai, son of the Maacathite; Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite;

verses.rationale: Follows read Hezrai and keeps Paarai.
verses.before: Hezro the Carmelite; Paarai the Arbite;
verses.after: Hezrai the Carmelite; Paarai the Arbite;
verses.tsw_comparator: Hezro the Carmelite; Paarai the Arbite;

verses.rationale: Retains both entries rather than importing the parallel list’s names.

verses.after: Igal son of Nathan from Zobah; Bani the Gadite;

verses.after: Zelek the Ammonite; Naharai the Beerothite, who carried the weapons of Joab son of Zeruiah;

verses.rationale: Keeps both Ithrites distinct.
verses.before: Ira the Ithrite; Gareb the Ithrite;
verses.after: Ira the Ithrite; Gareb the Ithrite;
verses.tsw_comparator: Ira the Ithrite; Gareb the Ithrite;

verses.rationale: Preserves the final Uriah name and stated total without forcing the preceding uncertain list to fit it.
verses.before: Uriah the Hittite. Thirty-seven in all.
verses.after: and Uriah the Hittite. Thirty-seven in all.
verses.tsw_comparator: Uriah the Hittite. Thirty-seven in all.

verses.rationale: Retains the source’s divine agency rather than harmonizing the parallel account’s adversary.
verses.before: Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he incited David against them, saying, “Go, count Israel and Judah.”
verses.after: Again the LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and he incited David against them, saying, “Go, count Israel and Judah.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he incited David against them, saying, “Go, count Israel and Judah.”

verses.rationale: Keeps full-land extent and David’s stated purpose.
verses.before: The king said to Joab, commander of the army who was with him, “Go now through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and count the people, so that I may know the number of the people.”
verses.after: The king told Joab, the army commander with him, “Please go through all Israel’s tribes, from Dan to Beer-sheba, and muster the people, so I may know their number.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king said to Joab, commander of the army who was with him, “Go now through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and count the people, so that I may know the number of the people.”

verses.rationale: Retains the hundredfold wish and challenge without adding an unstated legal explanation.
verses.before: Yet Joab said to the king, “May the LORD your God add to the people a hundred times as many as they are, while the eyes of my lord the king see it. But why does my lord the king delight in this thing?”
verses.after: Joab answered the king, “May the LORD your God multiply the people a hundred times over, while my lord the king sees it with his own eyes. But why does my lord the king delight in this?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Joab said to the king, “May the LORD your God add to the people a hundred times as many as they are, while the eyes of my lord the king see it. But why does my lord the king delight in this thing?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the officers’ overridden objection and compliance.
verses.before: Yet the king’s word prevailed against Joab and against the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army went out from before the king to count the people of Israel.
verses.after: But the king’s command prevailed over Joab and the army commanders. They left the king’s presence to muster the people of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet the king’s word prevailed against Joab and against the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army went out from before the king to count the people of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the compressed geographic sequence without pretending its syntax is certain.
verses.before: They crossed the Jordan and camped in Aroer, on the right side of the city that is in the middle of the wadi, toward Gad and toward Jazer.
verses.after: They crossed the Jordan and camped at Aroer, south of the town in the valley, in Gad, and toward Jazer.
verses.tsw_comparator: They crossed the Jordan and camped in Aroer, on the right side of the city that is in the middle of the wadi, toward Gad and toward Jazer.

verses.rationale: Retains the obscure pinned place names rather than reconstructing them from other witnesses.
verses.before: They came to Gilead and to the land of Tahtim-Hodshi. They came to Dan-Jaan and around to Sidon.
verses.after: They went to Gilead and the land of Tahtim-hodshi, then to Dan-jaan and around toward Sidon.
verses.tsw_comparator: They came to Gilead and to the land of Tahtim-Hodshi. They came to Dan-Jaan and around to Sidon.

verses.rationale: Preserves all named regions and peoples along the route.
verses.before: They came to the stronghold of Tyre and to all the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites, and they went out to the Negev of Judah at Beersheba.
verses.after: They came to the fortress of Tyre and all the towns of the Hivites and Canaanites, then went out to the Negeb of Judah at Beer-sheba.
verses.tsw_comparator: They came to the stronghold of Tyre and to all the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites, and they went out to the Negev of Judah at Beersheba.

verses.rationale: Retains the exact duration.
verses.before: They went throughout all the land and came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
verses.after: After going through the whole land, they returned to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
verses.tsw_comparator: They went throughout all the land and came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.

verses.rationale: Preserves Samuel’s two totals and its differing descriptions of the groups.
verses.before: Joab gave the number of the census of the people to the king: Israel was eight hundred thousand valiant men who drew the sword, and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.
verses.after: Joab gave the king the number of the people mustered: in Israel, eight hundred thousand fighting men who drew the sword, and in Judah, five hundred thousand men.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joab gave the number of the census of the people to the king: Israel was eight hundred thousand valiant men who drew the sword, and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.

verses.rationale: Keeps the striking-heart image, confession, and request without supplying the census’s unexpressed motive.
verses.before: David’s heart struck him after he had counted the people. David said to the LORD, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done. And now, O LORD, please cause the guilt of your servant to pass away, for I have acted very foolishly.”
verses.after: After David counted the people, his heart struck him. He said to the LORD, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done. Now, LORD, please take away your servant’s guilt, for I have acted very foolishly.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David’s heart struck him after he had counted the people. David said to the LORD, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done. And now, O LORD, please cause the guilt of your servant to pass away, for I have acted very foolishly.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both prophet and seer designations and introduces the message.
verses.before: When David arose in the morning, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Gad, David’s seer, saying,
verses.after: When David rose in the morning, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Gad, David’s seer:
verses.tsw_comparator: When David arose in the morning, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Gad, David’s seer, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps the threefold choice and divine action.
verses.before: “Go and speak to David: Thus says the LORD: Three things I am laying before you. Choose for yourself one of them, and I will do it to you.”
verses.after: “Go and tell David, ‘This is what the LORD says: I am laying three things before you. Choose one, and I will do it to you.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Go and speak to David: Thus says the LORD: Three things I am laying before you. Choose for yourself one of them, and I will do it to you.”

verses.rationale: Retains pinned seven years, three months, and three days rather than harmonizing the famine duration.
verses.before: So Gad came to David and told him and said to him, “Will seven years of famine come upon you in your land? Or will you flee three months before your adversaries while they pursue you? Or will there be three days of plague in your land? Now know and see what word I will return to the one who sent me.”
verses.after: Gad came to David and told him, “Shall seven years of famine come on your land? Or will you flee for three months before enemies who pursue you? Or shall there be three days of plague in your land? Now think carefully about what answer I should take to the one who sent me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Gad came to David and told him and said to him, “Shall seven years of famine come upon you in your land? Or will you flee three months before your adversaries while they pursue you? Or shall there be three days of plague in your land? Now know and see what word I shall return to the one who sent me.”

verses.rationale: Follows read mercies and preserves the deliberate us-to-me shift.
verses.before: David said to Gad, “I am in great distress. Please let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for his compassion is great, but let me not fall into the hand of humanity.”
verses.after: David told Gad, “I am in great distress. Please let us fall into the LORD’s hand, for his mercies are many. But do not let me fall into human hands.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to Gad, “I am in great distress. Please let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for his compassion is great, but let me not fall into the hand of humanity.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the unspecified appointed endpoint and full death count.
verses.before: So the LORD sent a plague upon Israel from the morning until the appointed time, and seventy thousand men from the people died, from Dan to Beersheba.
verses.after: So the LORD sent a plague on Israel from that morning until the appointed time. Seventy thousand people died, from Dan to Beer-sheba.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the LORD sent a plague upon Israel from the morning until the appointed time, and seventy thousand men from the people died, from Dan to Beersheba.

verses.rationale: Follows read Araunah and retains relenting, command, and the angel’s location.
verses.before: When the messenger stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, the LORD relented concerning the disaster and said to the messenger who was destroying among the people, “Enough! Now relax your hand.” And the messenger of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
verses.after: When the angel stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, the LORD relented from the disaster. He told the angel destroying the people, “Enough! Now withdraw your hand.” The LORD’s angel was beside the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the messenger stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, the LORD relented concerning the disaster and said to the messenger who was destroying among the people, “Enough! Now relax your hand.” And the messenger of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

verses.rationale: Keeps David’s repeated personal responsibility and the sheep image without changing it into a narrator’s innocence verdict.
verses.before: David spoke to the LORD when he saw the messenger who was striking the people and said, “Look, I am the one who sinned, and I am the one who acted perversely. But these sheep—what have they done? Please let your hand be against me and against my father’s house.”
verses.after: When David saw the angel striking the people, he said to the LORD, “I am the one who sinned; I am the one who did wrong. But these sheep—what have they done? Please let your hand fall on me and my father’s house.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David spoke to the LORD when he saw the messenger who was striking the people and said, “Look, I am the one who sinned, and I am the one who acted perversely. But these sheep—what have they done? Please let your hand be against me and against my father’s house.”

verses.rationale: Follows read name and preserves the new instruction.
verses.before: Gad came to David that day and said to him, “Go up, raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”
verses.after: That day Gad came to David and said, “Go up and raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Gad came to David that day and said to him, “Go up, raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the connection between prophetic word and divine command.
verses.before: So David went up according to the word of Gad, as the LORD commanded.
verses.after: David went up at Gad’s word, just as the LORD had commanded.
verses.tsw_comparator: So David went up according to the word of Gad, as the LORD commanded.

verses.rationale: Retains seeing, approach, and homage.
verses.before: Araunah looked down and saw the king and his servants crossing over toward him. Araunah went out and bowed down to the king with his face to the ground.
verses.after: Araunah looked out and saw the king and his servants approaching. He went out and bowed facedown to the ground before the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Araunah looked down and saw the king and his servants crossing over toward him. Araunah went out and bowed down to the king with his face to the ground.

verses.rationale: Keeps purchase and intended purpose distinct from the later free offer.
verses.before: Araunah said, “Why has my lord the king come to his servant?” David said, “To buy the threshing floor from you, to build an altar to the LORD, so that the plague may be restrained from the people.”
verses.after: Araunah asked, “Why has my lord the king come to his servant?” David answered, “To buy your threshing floor and build an altar to the LORD, so the plague may be stopped among the people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Araunah said, “Why has my lord the king come to his servant?” David said, “To buy the threshing floor from you, to build an altar to the LORD, so that the plague may be restrained from the people.”

verses.rationale: Preserves all offered materials and the agricultural implements.
verses.before: Araunah said to David, “Let my lord the king take and offer up what is good in his eyes. Look, the oxen for the burnt offering and the threshing sledges and the equipment of the oxen for the wood.
verses.after: Araunah told David, “Let my lord the king take and offer whatever is good in his eyes. Here are the cattle for the burnt offering, and the threshing sledges and cattle equipment for the wood.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Araunah said to David, “Let my lord the king take and offer up what is good in his eyes. Look, the oxen for the burnt offering and the threshing sledges and the equipment of the oxen for the wood.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult title attached to Araunah instead of silently deleting or relocating it into speech.
verses.before: All this, O king, Araunah gives to the king.” And Araunah said to the king, “May the LORD your God accept you.”
verses.after: Araunah the king gave all this to the king. Araunah said to the king, “May the LORD your God accept you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: All this, O king, Araunah gives to the king.” And Araunah said to the king, “May the LORD your God accept you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps emphatic purchase, cost, exact price, and scope rather than importing the parallel account’s amount.
verses.before: But the king said to Araunah, “No, but I will surely buy it from you for a price, for I will not offer to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
verses.after: But the king told Araunah, “No. I will certainly buy it from you for a price. I will not offer the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing floor and the cattle for fifty silver shekels.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the king said to Araunah, “No, but I will surely buy it from you for a price, for I will not offer to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

verses.rationale: Retains both offerings and the closing answered-plea formula linking the book’s final accounts.
verses.before: David built there an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and offerings of well-being. Then the LORD was entreated for the land, and the plague was restrained from Israel.
verses.after: David built an altar to the LORD there and offered burnt offerings and well-being offerings. The LORD responded to pleas for the land, and the plague was stopped in Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: David built there an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and offerings of well-being. Then the LORD was entreated for the land, and the plague was restrained from Israel.
